summary: The proposed allow resolves the reported false denial but also overrides destructive-command denies. FR-2 also conflicts with the required test file.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec.md FR-1 and acceptance criteria: The proposed allow also matches role-gate commands followed by ; rm x or && cp a b. Rationale: The later allow overrides existing word denies, but the spec says old deny cases stay denied and does not define this exception.
F2 [Blocker] spec.md FR-2 and FR-3: FR-2 forbids every other file change, but FR-3 requires a new test file. Rationale: Red cannot satisfy both requirements without choosing an exception.
evidence: HEAD and baseline match; the branch and initial working tree match the brief.
The v2_shell_effect helper returns deny for the reported heading and allow after the proposed insertion. The matching word deny is *rm *.
The helper returns allow for a chained destructive command and deny for a redirected command after the insertion. It evaluates the last matching rule, not the first.
The platform independently rejected a shell call containing a word-deny pattern; platform rule ordering was not independently verified.
Exactly eight agent files contain the word deny. Adversarial testing has shell allow and no word deny.
The runner discovers test_*.sh, and the required positive assertion fails at the current base. The named comparison commit exists.
commands: v2_shell_effect helper probe on original and in-memory proposed rules

paraphrase.proposes: Add a role-gate allow rule to eight audit roles after their word denies and before their redirection denies. Add a contract test for the reported heading and existing deny cases.
paraphrase.current_system: The audit roles allow shell commands, then deny several unanchored word patterns. A phase heading contains text that matches a deny pattern, so the role-gate command is denied.
